So the rate bounds causal recall from above but "does not generally identify it" (the bounds collapse to the observed recall when $p_0=0$, that is, when the target outcome never occurs in the control arm). pairs.old: [Guan et al. 2025](./#p=guan2025monitoring): $\text{g-mean}^2=\mathrm{TPR}\cdot\mathrm{TNR}$; in the intervention setting $\mathrm{TPR}_{\mathrm{mc}}=\min\{1,\Pr(Z=1\mid X=1,Y=1)/R_{\text{effect}}\}$ with $R_{\text{effect}}=\mathrm{TE}/\Pr(Y=1\mid X=1)$, and $\text{g-mean}^2=\mathrm{TPR}_{\mathrm{mc}}\sqrt{\mathrm{TNR}_{X=1}\,\mathrm{TNR}_{X=0}}$.
pairs.new: [Guan et al. 2025](./#p=guan2025monitoring) multiply the true-positive rate (TPR, the share of positive cases the monitor flags) by the true-negative rate (TNR, the share of negative cases it does not flag): $\text{g-mean}^2=\mathrm{TPR}\cdot\mathrm{TNR}$. In the intervention setting, $X=1$ marks the intervention arm and $X=0$ the control arm, $Y=1$ the target behavior and $Z=1$ a monitor flag. The minimal-criterion true-positive rate divides the monitor's flag rate on positive cases in the intervention arm by $R_{\text{effect}}$ and caps the result at 1. Here $R_{\text{effect}}$ is the total effect $\mathrm{TE}$ of the intervention (the difference in the rate of the target behavior between the intervention arm and the control arm) divided by the rate of the behavior in the intervention arm: $\mathrm{TPR}_{\mathrm{mc}}=\min\{1,\Pr(Z=1\mid X=1,Y=1)/R_{\text{effect}}\}$ with $R_{\text{effect}}=\mathrm{TE}/\Pr(Y=1\mid X=1)$. The score multiplies this rate by the geometric mean of the true-negative rates in the two arms: $\text{g-mean}^2=\mathrm{TPR}_{\mathrm{mc}}\sqrt{\mathrm{TNR}_{X=1}\,\mathrm{TNR}_{X=0}}$.

pairs.new: [Anonymous 2026 (improving monitorability)](./#p=anon2026improving) define causal recall with potential outcomes: $Y(1)$ and $Y(0)$ are the behavior the model would show with and without the intervention, and $Z(1)$ is the monitor's verdict with it. Causal recall is the probability of a flag among the cases in which the intervention caused the behavior: $r_c:=\Pr(Z(1)=1\mid U=1)$ with $U:=\mathbf{1}\{Y(1)=1,Y(0)=0\}$. With $R=(p_1-p_0)/p_1$, where $p_1$ and $p_0$ are the rates of the target outcome in the intervention and control arms, they bound causal recall using the observed true-positive rate $\mathrm{TPR}_{ob}$ (the monitor's flag rate on positive cases in the intervention arm) and $R$: $\max\{0,(\mathrm{TPR}_{ob}+R-1)/R\}\le r_c\le\min\{1,\mathrm{TPR}_{ob}/R\}$.

pairs.new: [Guan et al. 2025](./#p=guan2025monitoring) distinguish three types, which they call archetypes. Three papers restate this classification: [Anonymous 2026 (CoT reliance)](./#p=anon2026chainofthought), [Duzan & Cooper Stickland 2026](./#p=duzan2026chainofthought) and [OpenAI 2026](./#p=openai2026gpt6astra). pairs.old: These rows ask whether reasoning is accessible to four reader roles: a verifier with relaxed completeness and soundness ([Kirchner et al. 2024](./#p=kirchner2024proververifier)); a human matched to the prompter's language for legibility and expertise for coverage ([Emmons et al. 2025 (pragmatic)](./#p=emmons2025pragmatic)); a model reader assessed by continuation success ([Jiao et al. 2026](./#p=jiao2026tandem), [Roytburg et al. 2026](./#p=roytburg2026measuring)), prediction of trace tokens ([Jiao et al. 2026](./#p=jiao2026tandem)), or "final-answer agreement" ([Sullivan & Koller 2026](./#p=sullivan2026language)); and the monitor itself ([Baker et al. 2025](./#p=baker2025monitoring)).
pairs.new: These definitions ask whether the reasoning is accessible to one of four readers. The first is a verifier whose completeness (it accepts correct solutions) and soundness (it cannot be fooled into accepting incorrect ones) are required only in a relaxed form ([Kirchner et al. 2024](./#p=kirchner2024proververifier)). The second is a human with the same language as the person who wrote the prompt, for legibility, and the same expertise, for coverage ([Emmons et al. 2025 (pragmatic)](./#p=emmons2025pragmatic)). The third is a model, assessed by whether it can continue the reasoning successfully ([Jiao et al. 2026](./#p=jiao2026tandem), [Roytburg et al. 2026](./#p=roytburg2026measuring)), by how well it predicts the tokens of the trace ([Jiao et al. 2026](./#p=jiao2026tandem)), or by "final-answer agreement" ([Sullivan & Koller 2026](./#p=sullivan2026language)). The fourth is the monitor itself ([Baker et al. 2025](./#p=baker2025monitoring)).
